    {"name": "travel_related", "analytical_usefulness": 0.55, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "A useful flag but largely derivable from and redundant with asset_category_type=travel. Well grounded."},
    {"name": "high_value_asset_signal", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.55, "hallucination_observed": true, "rationale": "High-value flag is analytically relevant to declines, but there is an amount column that would ground value directly; here the signal is inferred from asset type/model rather than stated value, e.g. a generic Dell laptop flagged True while a service is False without price evidence."},
    {"name": "processing_lag_band", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Derived from processed_date vs opened_at; processing delay is a strong, actionable axis for reducing declines.     {"name": "asset_brand_family", "analytical_usefulness": 0.65, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Brand grouping offers a plausible segmentation, though less obviously tied to declines. Brands are correctly extracted from ci/description with sensible 'other' fallback."}

  "source_groundedness": 0.82,
  "rationale": "The added columns give multiple genuine analytical axes for a decline-reduction study: processing lag, submission origin, description/identifier quality, and asset categorisation are all actionable.
